name: Latveria Does Not Negotiate
notes: Nov 26, 2026: renamed Latveria Does Not Negotiate and cut down to three versions. Main list = The Iron Mask (your sleeved deck, Bracket 3, no Game Changers); versions: Latverian Black Market (bang-for-the-buck upgrades) and God Emperor Doom (Ideal). Deleted: Ideal no-GC (now God Emperor Doom), Budget, both Build-today lists, Bracket 4, Bracket 5 and Sleeved + 2 GC; backup in mtg-data decks/_retired/doom-unrivaled-2026-11-25.json.

Nov 26 rule: the only win con is Doom. Backups must be other ways to empty the library (Leveler, Inverter of Truth, Mirror of Fate, Doomsday, Tainted Pact, Demonic Consultation, Demonic Bargain); no drain or damage finishers. Demonic Bargain is in all three versions.
Nov 26: Cabal Ritual in for Treasure Map (Andrew's call: pairs with Dark Ritual for fast Doom turns; it's in every version).

3 Game Changer swaps (all owned): Demonic Tutor in for Tormod's Crypt, The One Ring in for Charcoal Diamond, Opposition Agent in for Ornithopter. Nov 26 sim, 4,000 games, Bracket 3 table: about 0.07 turns faster, i.e. nearly even. The sim doesn't model Opposition Agent stealing the table's tutors and fetches, and undersells the Ring, so the real gain is bigger against your table, not smaller. Check first: the Ring and Bowmasters were also floated for a Sauron B3 build.

The Iron Mask, Nov 26 sim, 4,000 games, Bracket 3 table: by turn 6 51%, turn 8 81%, turn 10 91%. Weakest slots in the sim: Victimize, Zombify, Buried Alive, Project Deathlok Soldier (the reanimation pile mostly overlaps Persist, Reanimate and Animate Dead). Removal reads as near-zero in a solitaire sim; kept on purpose for your interactive tables.
Lands: 37 all-unique names, so Tainted Pact works. Kept by choice: Duress, Adaptive Omnitool, Doomsday, Horn of Greed, Doomfall, Whispersilk Cloak.

Plan: Doom + Tainted Pact or Demonic Consultation (exile the library, tap Doom), Doom + Leveler or Inverter of Truth, with a pile of tutors to find them. Every card name appears once, so Tainted Pact works. Tell the table about the two-card wins before the game.

Line A: cast Doom off fast mana, give him haste (Lightning Greaves {2}, equip {0}; Lavaspur Boots {1}, equip {1}), then Demonic Consultation naming a card not in the deck, or Tainted Pact taking nothing, and tap Doom.

Line B: cast Doom and pass. At the end step of the player before you, cast Pact or Consultation (opponents may still have mana up). Doom is summoning sick until your turn starts, so tap him in your upkeep, before your draw.
Line C (when Doomsday is in the list): pile Street Wraith, Dark Ritual, Night's Whisper, Demonic Consultation, Spoils of the Vault; Doom must already be able to tap.
Line D: Mirror of Fate (tap, sacrifice, choose zero cards) empties the library. Inverter of Truth only empties it when your graveyard is empty.
Never cast Spoils of the Vault from a full library: you lose a life per exiled card and die before Doom can tap. Doom's 'win even at 0 life' only covers his own 1 life.
Sim caveats: solitaire model; opponents remove and block at fixed rates but don't race. Trust the differences between versions more than the raw turns. Prices are the Nov 12 card-data refresh.

History: Nov 8 merged build (Doom + Leveler, Ultron backup); Nov 10-18 Owned-build swaps; Nov 20 Unique Pact; Nov 21 sim-driven tiers (Ideal/Budget/Build today/B4/B5); Nov 22 sleeved list; Nov 26 three-version cleanup. Old lists are in the mtg-data repo.
source: Andrew's sleeved deck, matched Nov 25; Cabal Ritual added Nov 26

notes: Bang-for-the-buck upgrades from The Iron Mask: 12 spells plus 11 lands, about $114 total at the cheapest printings (Nov 12 prices).

Step 1, the cheap core (about $18.50, 0.58 turns faster on its own): The Cruelty of Gix ($1.31) for Tormod's Crypt, Inverter of Truth ($0.95) for Victimize, Dark Petition ($2.95) for Zombify, Scheming Symmetry ($8.01) for Buried Alive, Jeweled Amulet ($4.70) for Project Deathlok Soldier, Shambling Ghast ($0.33) for Isolinear Processor, Springleaf Drum ($0.25) for Persist.

Step 2, the tutor pack (about $87 more): Cruel Tutor ($11.75) for Deadly Dispute, Plunge into Darkness ($15.40) for Animate Dead, Insidious Dreams ($16.81) for Black Market Connections, Beseech the Mirror ($19.25) for Thran Dynamo, Grim Tutor ($23.81) for Nasty End.

Step 3, the under-$5 lands (about $7.55; Evolving Wilds you already own; 0.12 turns faster): Bojuka Bog ($1.42) for Big Apple, 3 a.m.; Castle Locthwain ($1.07) for Hidden Hideout; Ifnir Deadlands ($0.25) for Dakmor Salvage; Mirrex ($0.78) for Spawning Pool; Treasure Vault ($1.12) for Pelakka Predation; Peat Bog ($1.20) for Grand Coliseum; Ebon Stronghold ($0.38) for Baxter Building; Evolving Wilds (owned) for Daily Bugle Building; Leechridden Swamp ($0.76) for The Grey Havens; Mortuary Mire ($0.29) for Surveillance Room; The Dross Pits ($0.28) for Mishra's Foundry. Bojuka Bog matters most: Tormod's Crypt is gone here, and Bog on yourself empties your graveyard so Inverter of Truth empties the library. Fell the Profane ($5.47) just missed the cutoff. Still 37 unique names plus both basics for Evolving Wilds and Fabled Passage.
Nov 26 sim, 6,000 games, Bracket 3 table, with the lands: by turn 6 71%, turn 8 90%, turn 10 94%. About 0.9 turns faster than The Iron Mask for about $114, most of the way to God Emperor Doom.
Skipped on purpose: Mox Amber, The Soul Stone, Cavern of Souls, Urborg, Lake of the Dead, Urza's Saga, Mox Opal. Each adds under 0.1 turns for a lot of money.

3 Game Changer swaps (all owned): Demonic Tutor in for Murmuring Volume, The One Ring in for Charcoal Diamond, Opposition Agent in for Ornithopter. Sim: about even (Agent isn't modeled; the Ring is undersold). Tormod's Crypt is already gone here, so Demonic Tutor takes Murmuring Volume's slot instead.
Every card name appears once, so Tainted Pact works.

3 Game Changer slots (the sim's best three): Demonic Tutor ($58.61, owned) in for Mask of Memory, Vampiric Tutor ($44.32) in for Stargaze, Chrome Mox ($51.19) in for Murmuring Volume. Nov 26 sim: by turn 6 76%, turn 8 91%, about 0.2 turns faster than without them.
